TXA                             \ ...raised by its first row
    BPL raised
.up_cell                            \ X = the line, negative: a cell up for each 8
    LDA s_ptr
    SEC
    SBC #&80
    STA s_ptr
    LDA s_ptr + 1
    SBC #&02
    CMP #&40
    BCS up_in_ring
    ADC #&40
.up_in_ring
    STA s_ptr + 1
    TXA
    CLC
    ADC #8
    TAX
    BCC up_cell
.raised                             \ A = X = the line of the lowest byte drawn
    ORA s_ptr                       \ the record's address
    LDY #9
    STA (v_ptr),Y
    INY
    LDA s_ptr + 1
    STA (v_ptr),Y
    LDA v_ptr                       \ the cells after it
    CLC
    ADC #11
    STA v_ptr
    BCC save_on_page                \ C = 0 on the common path
    INC v_ptr + 1
    CLC                             \ (the page-crossing path: C was 1)
.save_on_page                       \ C = 0 here (TXA, TAY, EOR leave it)
    \ the data: the byte for line Y of the first cell is data[count - 1 - (line - Y)], so
    \ d_ptr = the column + 2 + count - 1 - line = col_ptr - 1 - line = col_ptr + (line EOR &FF) - &100
    TXA
    TAY                             \ Y = the line
candidates.new:
TXA                             \ ...raised by its first row
    BMI up_cell                     \ negative (about 1 column in 8): a cell up for each 8, out of line
.raised                             \ A = X = the line of the lowest byte drawn
    ORA s_ptr                       \ the record's address
    LDY #9
    STA (v_ptr),Y
    LDY #10                         \ (LDY, not INY: the BCC below must start its next instruction on a page)
    LDA s_ptr + 1
    STA (v_ptr),Y
    LDA v_ptr                       \ the cells after it
    CLC
    ADC #11
    STA v_ptr
    BCC save_on_page                \ C = 0 on the common path
    INC v_ptr + 1
    CLC                             \ (the page-crossing path: C was 1)
    BRA save_on_page                \ 65C02 opcode
.up_cell                            \ X = the line, negative: a cell up for each 8
    LDA s_ptr
    SEC
    SBC #&80
    STA s_ptr
    LDA s_ptr + 1
    SBC #&02                        \ C = 1 after this: the ring's high byte is 3 or more
    ORA #&40                        \ round the 16K: &3D-&3F (below the ring) -> &7D-&7F
    STA s_ptr + 1
    TXA
    SBC #&F8                        \ + 8 (C = 1); carry out when it reaches 0 or more
    TAX
    BCC up_cell
    BRA raised                      \ 65C02 opcode: A = X = the line
.save_on_page                       \ C = 0 here (TXA, TAY, EOR leave it)
    \ the data: the byte for line Y of the first cell is data[count - 1 - (line - Y)], so
    \ d_ptr = the column + 2 + count - 1 - line = col_ptr - 1 - line = col_ptr + (line EOR &FF) - &100
    TXA
    TAY                             \ Y = the line
candidates.summary: Take the rare up_cell block out of line so the hot path's BPL (taken, and crossing a page: 4 cycles) becomes a never-taken BMI (2); up_cell itself loses its CMP/BCS/ADC for one ORA #&40 and its CLC (C is 1 after the hi SBC). Same 54 bytes, save_on_page stays at the same address. Alternative to candidate 2 (overlaps it).
candidates.equivalence: Hot path (X >= 0): TXA; BMI not taken falls into .raised with A = X = line exactly as BPL raised arrived there; the rest is unchanged except LDY #10 for INY (same Y, same 2 cycles, one byte longer, used to start the BCC's next instruction at a page boundary). The page-crossing path gains BRA save_on_page after its CLC (it used to fall in; C = 0 as before). Rare path (X < 0): BMI to .up_cell, which does the same s_ptr -= &280 per 8 lines. ORA #&40 replaces CMP #&40/BCS/ADC #&40: after SBC #2 the high byte is &3D-&7F (ring high byte is &40-&7F; the same ORA #&40 is used at save_same_page), and for &3D-&3F ORA gives &7D-&7F = +&40, for &40-&7F it is unchanged. The SBC #2 cannot borrow (high byte >= &40), so C = 1 after it (ORA, STA, TXA leave C); X + 8 as SBC #&F8 with C = 1 gives the same A and the same carry out (set iff X >= &F8) as CLC/ADC #8, so BCC up_cell loops and falls out identically with C = 1, A = X = the line; BRA raised rejoins .raised with A = X. Registers at .raised and .save_on_page are the same as before on every path (Y is 8 on entry in both and reloaded at .raised). No other entry: .up_cell, .up_in_ring, .raised, .save_on_page are only referenced inside the window (grep), and .up_in_ring is gone.
candidates.relies_on: Page crossings (listing of the unshifted DEBUG_LIVES build, TXA at &9BE8): old BPL raised at &9BE9 crossed to &9C05 (taken 4 cycles, 8.27 a pass, profile shows 35.4 for 9.4 executions). New: BMI not taken; BCC save_on_page at &9BFE has its next instruction at &9C00 and its target &9C1C in the same page (the LDY #10 padding byte makes that so; with INY the BCC would cross and lose 9.3 a pass). save_on_page stays at &9C1C so nothing after the window moves (54 bytes before and after). Rare path costs BMI taken (crosses) + BRA back (about +6 per up_cell entry, 1.13 a pass), counted in the claim. Measured on a scratch copy (unshifted DEBUG_LIVES, seed 1, 400 passes from 500, pcprof render phase): 18774.6 -> 18757.4 cycles a pass (-17.2); passlock vs the control 3000 passes, state and screen identical. Relies on the ring high byte being >= 3 (C = 1 after SBC #2), as save_same_page already does, and on code before &9BE8 not moving (another candidate before it in the same batch can undo the alignment).

candidates.summary: Smaller change: keep BPL raised, but up_cell loses CMP/BCS/ADC for ORA #&40 and its CLC (SBC #&F8 with C = 1). 5 bytes smaller, so the code after the window slides down 5. BPL still crosses a page (raised at &9C00, BPL's next instruction &9BEB). Alternative to candidate 1 (overlaps it).
candidates.equivalence: Only .up_cell changes. ORA #&40 equals CMP #&40/BCS/ADC #&40 for a high byte after SBC #2 of &3D-&7F (ring high byte >= &40); the SBC #2 cannot borrow so C = 1, and X + 8 as SBC #&F8 gives the same A and carry out as CLC; ADC #8. Exits with C = 1, A = X = the line as before. .up_in_ring removed (only referenced inside the window).
candidates.relies_on: Shortens the block 26 -> 21 bytes so everything after it moves down 5 bytes: moves BPL raised's target from &9C05 to &9C00 (still a page cross, so still 4 cycles taken) and every later address by 5; page crossings of later branches/indexed reads are not checked. Measured on a scratch copy (pcprof render phase, seed 1, 400 passes): 18774.6 -> 18771.7 (-2.9).
